text:
Aisha: Hey team — I’m Aisha, just finished accounts. First-week bootstrapping question: WSL2 (Win11) + VSCode Remote + devcontainer + asdf for node/python. Git pushes from inside the devcontainer error with Permission denied (publickey). Outside the container (in WSL) ssh works fine. Inside container SSH_AUTH_SOCK is unset. Using Git Credential Manager on Windows. Any tips?

Aisha: My quick snippets:
```bash
# ~/.ssh/config (WSL)
Host *
  AddKeysToAgent yes
  ForwardAgent yes
  IdentityFile ~/.ssh/id_ed25519

# devcontainer.json (partial)
"runArgs": ["--init", "-v", "/home/vscode/.ssh:/home/vscode/.ssh:ro"]
```

Sam (onboarding): welcome! :wave: Most likely socket forwarding issue across Win -> WSL -> container. Did you try enabling agent forwarding in VSCode settings (Remote.SSH > Enable Agent Forwarding) and also set the container to mount the host agent socket?

Maya (eng-infra): echoing Sam. Windows' OpenSSH uses a named pipe; WSL exposes a unix socket at /run/host-services/ssh-auth.sock on newer Windows builds. When the container runs, it doesn't get that by default. Two quick approaches:
1) Use npiperelay/wsl-ssh-agent so Windows agent is proxied to a unix socket in WSL, then bind-mount that socket into the container. Example: use the wsl-ssh-agent package or npiperelay to create /run/host-services/ssh-auth.sock.
2) Start an ssh-agent inside WSL, add your key there (eval \"$(ssh-agent -s)\" && ssh-add ~/.ssh/id_ed25519) and mount that agent socket into the container.

Maya (eng-infra): minimal socat-ish sketch (run in WSL):
```bash
# create a host-visible socket and forward to Windows pipe (example, adapt to your npiperelay path)
/usr/bin/npiperelay.exe -ep -s \\\\.\\\\pipe\openssh-ssh-agent > /run/host-services/ssh-auth.sock &
chmod 600 /run/host-services/ssh-auth.sock
# then start container with: -v /run/host-services/ssh-auth.sock:/ssh-agent -e SSH_AUTH_SOCK=/ssh-agent
```
(If you use npiperelay binaries from scoop/choco, restart WSL after install: `wsl --shutdown`.)

Jun (devex): also check Git Credential Manager. If GCM is handling creds and falling back to https, it may still want an SSH key for some repos. You can debug push auth with: `GCM_LOG=1 GCM_TRACE=1 git push` or temporarily try `git clone git@github.com:org/repo.git` from inside the container to see the SSH error. If you see \"agent refused\" that's the socket/forwarding issue.

Sam (onboarding): If you prefer an easier path for now, create a deploy key on the repo and add it to the container (~/.ssh/id_deploy) and set repo-specific config while we sort agent forwarding. Not ideal long-term but low-friction for first-day tasks.

deploy-bot: dotfiles-skel applied to /home/aisha (ran by Sam) :white_check_mark:

Aisha: Tried npiperelay + mounting /run/host-services/ssh-auth.sock into the devcontainer and restarted VSCode. Also re-added key with ssh-add inside WSL. After that, git push from inside container works. Thank you all! :tada:

Aisha: Notes for my dotfiles: added asdf plugin commands I ran:
```bash
asdf plugin-add nodejs https://github.com/asdf-vm/asdf-nodejs.git || true
asdf install nodejs 18.17.1
asdf global nodejs 18.17.1
asdf plugin-add python
asdf install python 3.11.6
asdf global python 3.11.6
```

Maya (eng-infra): glad that worked. If you want, open a short PR to the onboarding dotfiles README with the npiperelay steps so future Windows folks have it documented.

Aisha: Will do and ping you for review, thanks!
